title: Etale sheaves over an algebraically closed field are constant
statement: Let $\Omega$ be an algebraically closed field and let $G$ be a sheaf of sets on the small etale site $(\operatorname{Spec}\Omega)_{\Et}$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets]. The canonical morphism from the constant sheaf with value $\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}\Omega,G)$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] to $G$ is an isomorphism, naturally in $G$. Under the identity geometric point $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, this isomorphism identifies $\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}\Omega,G)$ with the geometric stalk $G_{\mathrm{id}}$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks].

source.place: Remark 59.23.2 (Tag 03P5, remark-constant-locally-constant-maps), together with the description of the etale site of Spec of a separably closed field used in Lemma 59.39.3 (Tag 0A3H)

proof.text: Let U be an object of (Spec Omega)_Et. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points] to U \to Spec Omega and its unique base point shows that every point of U is open and that its residue field is a finite separable extension of Omega. Since Omega is algebraically closed, each residue field is Omega. Thus U is the coproduct of its open one-point subschemes, each canonically a copy of Spec Omega; the empty object is allowed as the empty coproduct.

source.place: Lemma 02GL (Tag 02GL), part (1) and its application to U -> Spec Omega

proof.text: Write U = coproduct_i Spec Omega for the decomposition of Step 1. The singleton pieces form an etale covering of U, and all pairwise overlaps are empty. The sheaf equalizer condition therefore identifies G(U) with the product of the sets G(Spec Omega), one factor for each piece; restriction along a morphism of etale objects is the corresponding pullback of the family. This also covers the empty coproduct, whose section set is a singleton.

source.place: Remark 03P5 (Tag 03P5), sheafification by locally constant maps, specialized to the discrete decomposition of an etale Omega-scheme

proof.text: Let A = Gamma(Spec Omega, G). The constant sheaf with value A has, on the same decomposition U = coproduct_i Spec Omega, exactly the same product of copies of A: on each connected one-point piece its sections are A, by [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-set-sections-connected-natural], and the sheaf equalizer gives the product over the pieces. The canonical morphism from the constant sheaf to G is therefore a bijection on sections of every U, since its component on each piece is the identity map A \to G(Spec Omega)=A. Hence it is an isomorphism of sheaves, and the construction is natural in G.

source.place: Remark 03P5 (Tag 03P5), locally constant maps and constant sheafification

proof.text: For the identity geometric point, the pointed object (Spec Omega, id) is a terminal object among pointed etale neighbourhoods of the identity: every pointed neighbourhood has its structure morphism from Spec Omega, and the point condition makes it unique. Thus the colimit defining the geometric stalk is canonically G(Spec Omega), and the isomorphism of Step 3 identifies A with G_id by the germ of a global section. This identification is natural in G.

source.place: Definition of geometric stalks preceding Lemma 03Q1 (Tag 03Q1), specialized to the identity point
